To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) when people are motivated to touch a product, they are more likely to be persuaded by a message that incorporates touch, (b) when people are not motivated to engage in the touch experience, they are more persuaded by a message when they can make sense of how touch is related to a message, and (c) when people are more motivated to touch, they are more affected by the touch and more persuaded by a communication incorporating touch.
touch has a positive influence on attitudes and behavior when people are motivated to touch for the fun of it, and that touch is also effective when people can make sense of the touch.
touch can be an effective persuasion tool when the touch is fun, interesting, or related to the message and when the sensory feedback of the touch is neutral or positive.
